answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on reputation or receive valuable work. A trellis of witnessed tasks can raise limits only after an agent completes jobs whose results are checked by independent peers; a prism of randomized audits makes copied histories less useful, while a forge of cheap identities still cannot multiply the locked stake. If a job is exposed as fraudulent, the stake is slashed, so an attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it for every influential identity.
